title: Accept and read Krisis decision accounts
summary: Idempotently accept immutable Krisis accounts into one explicitly identified decisions library and read its bounded accepted-account feed.
use_when: Krisis must hand one deterministic decision account to its configured Annals decisions library.
A local consumer must freeze or page the accepted-account prefix without reading raw account Markdown.
do_not_use_when: General source material should enter the primary Annals inbox.
A caller wants to review, rank, supersede, retract, delete, or determine the current force of a decision.
The decisions-library config and exact expected persistent library ID are unavailable.
outcome: One durable producer acceptance and unstarted inbox job, an exact idempotent replay, or a bounded immutable feed view fixed to a requested watermark.
effects: First acceptance copies unchanged account bytes into a complete producer-identified inbox envelope and appends one immutable acceptance row.

A decision-config inbox run binds only a fresh empty spool or verifies its existing binding, ignores ordinary incoming files, and dispatches only committed producer-accepted originals or their explicit retry children.
Exact replay and feed reads are side-effect free; conflicting bytes, invalid input, maintenance, insufficient storage, or identity mismatch create no acceptance.
Acceptance starts no source delivery, model run, reconciliation, or corpus transition; later inbox dispatch retains its separate existing effects.
authority: Krisis owns decision identification, producer key, account meaning, bounded content, and source anchors.
Annals owns the configured library and spool identity, accepted bytes, producer idempotency, job identity, event order, and feed projection.
A feed event reports acceptance, not objective truth, semantic relevance, processing success, or current force.
success: A created or replayed receipt identifies contract version, exact library, producer, key, SHA-256, stable original job, and acceptance time without content or paths.
A page echoes the requested watermark and cursor, returns ascending immutable events, and leaves an empty-page cursor unchanged.
Concurrent identical calls converge on one acceptance and concurrent different-byte calls have at most one winner.
failure_and_recovery: Retry an ambiguous acceptance only with the identical producer key and bytes; never mint a replacement key because dispatch failed.
If envelope publication completed before an uncertain database commit, the next identical call reconstructs the acceptance from that envelope.
Treat missing or mismatched config, schema, library identity, spool identity, envelope, or digest as a closed boundary; do not redirect or edit receipts.
privacy: Complete accounts remain private in Krisis handoff state and the Annals decisions spool, library, archives, and backups; model dispatch may later disclose relevant decisions-library context only through the separate inbox contract.
Feed output omits raw Markdown, authority quotation, transcript, paths, diffs, commands, tool output, prompts, credentials, and general-library content.
does_not_authorize: Release, installation, provisioning, migration, activation, historical import, publication, remote sharing, direct SQLite or spool editing, deletion, pruning, or storage cleanup.
Using the primary library, changing the configured target per account, or treating local producer routing as authentication against the local user.
Consumer acknowledgement, correction, retraction, review, confidence, disposition, supersession, relationship, semantic relevance, or current-force state.

consumers.statement: Krisis may submit one immutable schema-one Markdown account per decision, and local consumers may read the resulting accepted-account prefix.

preconditions.statement: Every exchange command names one explicit decisions config containing a library, inbox root, and exact 32-lowercase-hex expected library ID; the current schema, persistent library identity, and immutable decisions role must match, and acceptance or dispatch binds or verifies the spool identity.
New acceptance additionally requires no deployment maintenance and enough spool headroom to preserve the configured reserve.

inputs.statement: Acceptance takes producer krisis, one nonblank producer key, and one regular non-symbolic nonblank UTF-8 Markdown file of at most 1 MiB with the ordered schema-one account sections and metadata.
A page takes one committed watermark, one earlier watermark or item cursor, and a limit from 1 through 200.

outputs.statement: Acceptance JSON reports contract_version, library_id, producer, key, source_sha256, job_id, accepted_at, and acceptance created or replayed.
Watermark JSON reports contract and library identity plus an opaque token; page JSON echoes library, watermark, request_cursor and next_cursor and returns bounded accepted-account events.

data_semantics.statement: Producer acceptance means Annals durably owns one exact complete spool copy and the immutable producer tuple; it is not source-delivery, processing, reconciliation, corpus, truth, relevance, or current-force success.

Each feed event projects the account ID, schema, statement, context, action, result, Unix occurrence time and precision, and exactly one host/thread/turn/item/span authority anchor without returning raw account bytes.

identity_and_units.statement: Producer idempotency is scoped by persistent library ID, immutable decisions role, producer krisis, and producer key; SHA-256 binds exact bytes, job ID binds the original queue item, and event and cursor values are opaque.
Occurrence time is signed Unix seconds paired with producer precision; authority span is a nonempty unsigned byte range; file and page bounds are bytes and event count respectively.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A watermark freezes every committed acceptance through one sequence; pages return the ascending prefix strictly after the requested cursor and no later than that watermark.
No historical Decisions rows, negative decision coverage, raw account body, dispatch result, semantic interpretation, correction, retraction, or consumer acknowledgement appears in feed version one.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the local Annals CLI with an explicit decisions config; acceptance permits only producer krisis and feed commands are read-only.

With decision_feed configured, direct work add or integration, generic enqueue, ordinary incoming registration, and backlog import are rejected; the decisions database rejects those generic source paths even through another config, spool, or direct selector; dispatch permits accepted originals and explicit retry children.
Library override, environment or frontend fallback, direct SQLite access, receipt editing, cross-library query, and remote access are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: First acceptance publishes one complete unstarted envelope before committing its event; exact replay returns the original result, changed bytes conflict without mutation, and publication uncertainty is recovered from the envelope.
Pages are fixed to one watermark, strictly ascending, replay a committed prefix after uncertainty, and preserve the exact request cursor when empty; Annals keeps no consumer cursor.

operational_limits.statement: One call accepts one file of at most 1 MiB; one page returns 1 through 200 requested events; new spool copies preserve the configured available-byte reserve.
No acceptance, queue, dispatch, model, storage, schedule, throughput, quality, or wall-clock service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Exchange contract version 1, account schema 1, library schema 5, producer receipt 1, feed cursor 1, provider release, and later inbox or Nucleus protocols are distinct compatibility axes.
Changed accepted bytes, correction, retraction, or a new event type cannot be introduced under this version-one identity.

reliances.statement: Acceptance and feed reads invoke no Conversations, Nucleus, Clockwork, model, network, or remote service; later dispatch has its own declared Nucleus reliance.
